annotation.authors_or_issuer: Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications (MIC); Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI), Japan
annotation.venue: METI website (AI Guidelines for Business, summary slides)
named_instruments_referenced: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI
annotation.summary_en: Slide summary of Japan's voluntary AI Guidelines for Business Ver1.1 (MIC and METI). It sets ten common guiding principles and role-specific duties for AI developers, providers and business users. It takes a risk-based, agile-governance approach and incorporates the Hiroshima Process for advanced AI. It has no robotics-specific provisions.
key_provisions_or_claims: Ten common guiding principles: human-centric, safety, fairness, privacy, security, transparency, accountability, literacy, fair competition, innovation.
Separate obligations for AI developers, AI providers and AI business users across the lifecycle.
Incorporates Hiroshima Process guiding principles and code of conduct for advanced AI systems.
Voluntary, risk-based, living document with multi-stakeholder updating and agile governance.
Calls for management-led AI governance and value-chain and risk-chain cooperation.
